topic: A Karama cancels one use, not the whole phase

statements.text: The original Q&A blocks all Atreides auction inspections.
A Karama stops one use of an ability, using one Voice in one battle as its example.
The revised text aligns to the updated CHOAM replacement card.

decision: Cancel a single use. Apply one battle cancellation before plans are revealed.
reason: The official November clarification and subsequent replacement-card wording address the old phase-wide text directly.

review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Fremen Karama worm creates a Nexus

statements.text: The base Q&A says the Karama worm does not signal a Nexus.
The Karama worm causes a Nexus at the end of Spice Blow and Nexus.
The compilation preserves both contradictory answers.

decision: The special Fremen worm creates a phase-end Nexus.
reason: The later official answer explicitly addresses this exact card effect and timing.

review.assessment: Supported, exact special-worm later official correction; phase-end applies this special effect.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Advanced Fremen cannot move through storm

statements.text: Reserve placement into permitted storm sectors is allowed at half loss; movement and riding into or out of storm are forbidden.
Earlier FAQ and emailed rulings permit movement into or through storm.

decision: Permit legal reserve placement with half losses. Forbid ordinary movement and worm riding into or out of storm.
reason: The November answer specifically distinguishes placement from movement. Earlier answers describe an older interpretation.

review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Storm deck is conditional on Advanced Fremen

statements.text: The last two wheel users dial 1 to 3 on later turns.
Advanced Fremen selects a Storm Card for later turns.
The revised book explicitly always uses the Storm Deck for convenience.

decision: Without Advanced Fremen, retain the official dialed movement. With Advanced Fremen, use its Storm Cards after turn one.
reason: The revised book identifies its change as an intentional convenience house rule.

review.assessment: Supported, original conditional Fremen card ability over convenience house change.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

statements.text: If newly allied forces share a territory, the later player must leave if the earlier one has not.
The same evacuation rule applies to Bene Gesserit advisors sharing with an ally.
The revised book instead enforces separation after each individual turn and exempts advisors, acknowledging both departures.

decision: Use the official later-player evacuation rule, including Bene Gesserit advisors, except for Ecaz Occupy.
reason: Advisors have many exemptions, but the official clarification expressly includes them in the alliance constraint.

review.assessment: Supported, explicit official ally advisor evacuation rule; Ecaz exception remains.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Emperor pays an ally then receives its normal card payment

statements.text: The Emperor contribution goes to the ally and is paid back to the Emperor.
The unofficial text sends an Emperor purchase contribution directly to the Bank unless given first through its separate gift ability.

decision: Keep the official payment loop and immediate spice gifting ability.
reason: Do not silently adopt the revised economic change. The official answer is explicit, even if it makes the Emperor-funded purchase effectively free.

review.assessment: Supported, explicit official Emperor payment loop despite unofficial economic alternative.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Priority between Fremen and Guild special victory

statements.text: Fremen wins if no faction has won by the end of the last turn and its condition is met.
Guild wins if no faction has won by the end of play.
Collected answers disagree about Guild-first, Fremen-first and unconditional Fremen defaults.

decision: After normal victory checks, resolve a satisfied Fremen Special Victory Condition, then the Guild stall victory.
reason: The specific Fremen territorial test should do work rather than being made unreachable whenever the Guild plays. This is an interpretation of conflicting general special-victory language, not an uncontested explicit priority rule.

review.assessment: Supported medium, specific conditional Fremen victory must remain meaningful before general Guild stall win.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: No-Guild printed fallback differs from named Fremen special victory

statements.text: If no winner at game end and Guild absent, Fremen wins; if also absent, most strongholds wins with ties shared.
The named Fremen condition requires specific territories.

decision: Retain the printed no-Guild Fremen fallback as a separate end-game rule, without claiming its territorial test was met.
reason: Both official statements can be shown without erasing the explicit no-Guild fallback. Correct Bene Gesserit prediction does not target this fallback.

review.assessment: Supported medium, explicit printed fallback is distinct from named special territorial test.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

statements.text: When several factions meet the winning count, they tie unless the group chooses another whole turn.
The unofficial text awards the win to an unallied player with more strongholds before its shared-win clause.

decision: Share simultaneous qualifying victory; do not rank qualifying players by extra strongholds.
reason: The official question directly handles added strongholds from expansions and says tie.

review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Fremen ally revival is three free within its limit

statements.text: A faction normally cannot revive more than three forces per turn.
Fremen may allow its allies to revive three forces for free.
The revised text increases the ally free revival to three.
Collected material contains a reading that adds three to the ally normal revivals.

decision: Treat the benefit as three free revivals within the applicable total limit, not three additional forces.
reason: Unlike Emperor, Fremen does not state extra revivals or a new total limit. Tleilaxu or another explicit effect can raise the limit.

review.assessment: Supported medium, three free is a rate, not additional allowance; other explicit limits remain.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Revival eligibility of a dead Kwisatz Haderach

statements.text: If killed it must be revived like any other leader; its status does not affect other Atreides revival.
The revised summary allows its revival before all leaders die.
Designer reading requires normal leader eligibility; a community reading permits any Revival Phase.

decision: Pay two spice when normal Atreides leader revival is allowed, or use an explicit Ghola/Tleilaxu exception.
reason: The ordinary-leader wording supplies eligibility. The separate token does not prevent the five actual leaders from becoming eligible.

review.assessment: Supported medium, direct designer normal leader eligibility plus explicit exception sources.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Earlier surviving leaders and a later lasgun-shield explosion

statements.text: Surviving leaders remain in the battle territory until other battles finish.
An explosion destroys spice and all forces, including uninvolved forces.
The revised book explicitly includes previously used leaders in subsequent territory-wide effects.
Collected designer, relayed and community interpretations disagree whether earlier leaders die.
Direct Jack Reda answer after designer discussion says previously used leaders are not killed; this corrects the earlier informal Bill Eberle answer.

decision: A later lasgun-shield explosion does not kill leaders that survived an earlier battle in that territory.
reason: The collected direct Jack Reda ruling after designer discussion explicitly corrects the earlier informal interpretation. Leader discs left on the board mark their one-territory commitment; they do not become participants in a later battle.

review.assessment: Corrected, final direct designer consensus excludes earlier surviving leaders from later explosion.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Harkonnen special Karama exchanges at most four cards

statements.text: The original special power takes any number up to an entire hand.
The direct explanation says up to four; a following hand-limit answer loosely says all cards.
The revised faction entry sets a four-card maximum.

decision: Use up to four random cards during Bidding; temporary hand size may exceed eight, followed by an equal return.
reason: Use the specific quantitative rule over the loose all-cards phrase in the hand-limit answer. This matters against an expanded hand limit.

review.assessment: Supported medium, specific up-to-four quantitative answer controls loose all-card shorthand.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

statements.text: The base book includes Bribery after Basic alliances.
The designers state bribery should be Advanced and future rules will reflect this.

decision: Place binding paid deals and spice bribery in the Advanced chapter. Retain voluntary information sharing in either game.
reason: This adopts the explicit published design-intent correction. The FAQ expresses intended placement rather than pretending the older printed chapter was elsewhere.

review.assessment: Supported medium, explicit published design-intent note identifies bribery as Advanced.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Notes about cards remain an Atreides privilege

statements.text: Only Atreides may keep written records about cards.
General notes may be kept and mentions public card knowledge before a tournament caveat.

decision: Allow general notes, while reserving written Treachery Card tracking to Atreides.
reason: Keep the explicit faction privilege meaningful rather than extending a general note answer into its specific protected subject.

review.assessment: Supported medium, specific Atreides card-note privilege retained alongside general notes.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

statements.text: A revealed worm creates a Nexus at the end of the phase.
The Advanced sequence says resolve a Nexus after pile A then repeat for B.
The Fremen special worm causes a Nexus at phase end.
The revised Advanced sequence resolves a Nexus after each pile.

decision: Resolve pile A completely, including its Nexus and Fremen rides, then do the same for pile B. Two Nexus opportunities can occur. Fremen special Karama keeps its separately stated phase-end timing.
reason: The specific Advanced procedure expressly instructs a Nexus before the second card is revealed. It outweighs the general Basic phase-end summary. Independent review corrected the draft single-window normalization; no collected designer override supports that normalization.

review.assessment: Corrected after review: specific Advanced per-pile Nexus sequence prevails; original single-phase synthesis unsupported.
review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

topic: Replacement cards replace, not add copies

statements.text: Two updated Karama replace core copies; Poison Tooth and Artillery Strike replace Ixian copies, or can be added if that expansion is absent.
Discard errata changes use of Poison Tooth and Artillery Strike.

decision: Use corrected card designs with the official copy count, never duplicate old and replacement editions in the same deck.
reason: This is an explicit replacement instruction rather than a balance choice.

review.scope: Independent core manuscript and base-faction review, with the two-reviewer 402-comment audit recorded separately.

statements.text: Players independently and secretly dial, then reveal together.
Community disagrees whether independent dials forbid coordinating through deals.

decision: Keep the simultaneous secret choice procedure without inventing an additional ban on legal Advanced deals about the number.
reason: The general public binding-deal permission has no storm exception. Independent selection and simultaneous reveal still determine the actual numbers.

review.evidence: Base rulebook PDF pp7,12; collected FAQ comment index320, https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2284#issuecomment-6225671375; content/gf9/faq-review.json#coreJudgementReview
review.assessment: Supported at medium confidence. Independent simultaneous dials prescribe how each player chooses and reveals a number. The broad Advanced verbal-deal permission has no supplied storm-specific exception; preserve public legal deals without adding a coordination ban. Community disagreement leaves this an interpretation.
review.scope: Independent re-read of both official passages and the full collected disputed comment; no online re-verification or mechanics edit.

statements.text: Advanced Karama table says Guild must go in turn order when attempting to change its turn.
Community disagrees between normal-order restriction and stopping only one retryable attempt.

decision: Guild takes its normal storm-order turn after cancellation; it cannot retry out-of-order timing later that turn.
reason: The official table explicitly describes the resulting normal-order action. A retry would avoid the cancellation without giving up any resource.

review.evidence: Independent reviewer finding against Ixians & Tleilaxu PDF page 12, Advanced Karama table; collected FAQ comment 6225368442.
review.assessment: Normal storm-order turn is the explicit official result; a retryable out-of-order attempt would evade the cancellation.
review.scope: This interaction reviewed directly; not a certification of every source citation.
